# Compute the Area of Circle using Encapsulation

#### Course: Learn Java OOP

## Compute the Area of Circle using Encapsulation

In this example, we will compute the area of a circle using the concepts of encapsulation. Here, we will use the following formula.

```java
Area of a circle = 3. 14 * radius * radius
```

### Thought Process

From the formula, we know that we need the radius to calculate the area. Here, we will be using the private field radius, so that it cannot be directly modified from the outer class.

```java
class Area {
    private double radius;
}
```

We will then use the setter and getter method to modify and access the value of radius from outside.

```java
// setter method
public void setRadius(double radius) {
    
}
```

```java
// getter method
public double getRadius()

}
```

However, inside the setter method, we will use the condition to prevent radius from being negative.

```java
public void setRadius(double radius) {

    if (radius > 0) {
        this.radius = radius;
    }
    else {
        System.out.println("Radius is negative");
    }
}
```

Now, this code ensures that radius can't be negative.

Let's complete this program.

```java
1import java.util.Scanner;
2
3class Area {
4
5    private double radius;
6
7    // setter method
8    public void setRadius(double radius) {
9        
10        if (radius > 0) {
11            this.radius = radius;
12        }
13        else {
14            System.out.println("Radius is negative");
15        }
16    }
17
18    // getter method
19    public double getRadius() {
20        return this.radius;
21    }
22}
23
24class Main {
25
26    public static void main(String[] args) {
27
28        // object of Area class
29        Area area = new Area();
30        
31        // get radius input
32        System.out.println("Enter the value of radius:");
33        Scanner input = new Scanner(System.in);
34        double radius = input.nextDouble();
35        
36        // set value of private radius using setter
37        area.setRadius(radius);
38
39        // access the value of radius and compute the area
40        double circleArea = 3.14 * area.getRadius() * area.getRadius();
41        System.out.println("Area of Circle: " + circleArea);
42    }
43}
```

Sample Output 1

```text
Enter the value of radius:
8
Area of Circle: 200.96
```

Sample Output 2

```text
Enter the value of radius:
-8
Radius is negative
Area of Circle: 0.0
```

The program only assigns the value to radius, if it is not negative. Otherwise, the default value of double 0.0 will be assigned to radius. This way we can control the program by not letting users enter negative values.
